metadata.title: Comprehensive knowledge base for discharged soldiers – Momentum Companion
metadata.disclaimer: Amounts and conditions are estimates based on official sources (October–November 2026). Always verify with the Discharged Soldiers Department and Fund, National Insurance (Bituach Leumi) and the Tax Authority.
metadata.purpose: Central knowledge base for the Transition Companion – for the companion, its pages and agents
metadata.source: Discharged Soldiers Department and Fund, National Insurance, Israel Tax Authority

discharge_grant.description: A sum of money transferred automatically to your bank account. There are no restrictions on how you use it.
discharge_grant.eligibility: At least 12 months of service, or discharge for medical reasons after any length of service.
discharge_grant.timing: Within 60 days of discharge. Lone soldiers – an advance within 14 days.
discharge_grant.notes: Training months are sometimes classified as combat support or other. The amount appears in your personal area.

personal_deposit.description: Savings built up during your service. Can be used for approved purposes for 5 years.
approved_uses: Academic or vocational studies (including psychometric prep)
Buying an apartment, house or land
personal_deposit.after_5_years: The balance becomes free to use for any purpose
personal_deposit.how_to_claim: Through the personal area on the Department and Fund website
personal_deposit.timing: Available from the 14th day after discharge
personal_deposit.scam_warning: Do not pay any company that offers to "release your deposit early" — it is illegal. The deposit is used only through the personal area on the Department's website, free of charge.

tax_credit_points.how_to_claim: Form 101 with your employer, or tax coordination
tax_credit_points.not_automatic: Tax credit points are not automatic — you must request them on Form 101 with your employer.
tax_credit_points.refund: If you did not request them in time, you can ask the Tax Authority for a tax refund later.

bituach_leumi_exemption.name_he: Temporary exemption from National Insurance and health tax
bituach_leumi_exemption.duration: Two months after the month of discharge

preferred_work_grant.eligibility: Usually 24 months of service + work in approved sectors
preferred_work_grant.work_period: 6 full months of work or 150 working days
preferred_work_grant.description: A one-time grant for those who worked 6 full months (or 150 working days) full-time in defined sectors.

public_transport_free.how: Update the "discharged soldier" profile on your Rav-Kav card or in the app.
public_transport_free.important: You must validate every ride, even though it is free.

arnona.notes: Full arnona exemption for up to 4 months from discharge from mandatory service, on 70 m² (90 m² with 5+ residents). Only for an apartment you own or rent — not your parents' home. Request it from the local authority.

unemployment.notes: Possible unemployment benefit in the first year, provided you worked at least 6 months (up to 6 months of service can be counted).

mimadim_lelimudim.description: Funding of up to 100% of university tuition for a first degree or certificate studies in the arts.
eligibility: Combat soldiers with an honourable ('gold') discharge
mimadim_lelimudim.deadline: First application within 5 years of discharge (sometimes longer)
mimadim_lelimudim.notes: No volunteering hours required. Registration opens every year.

periphery_scholarships.description: Funding of the first year for residents of the periphery / priority areas.

mechina_bagrut.description: Funding or significant subsidy for pre-academic preparatory programs and completing matriculation exams.

practical_engineering.description: High partial funding at recognised institutions.

psychometric.notes: Sometimes fully or partly funded through the deposit or other benefits.

cv_tips: Translate military skills into civilian language
Highlight responsibility, teamwork, working under pressure, management

common_translations.Combat soldier: Working under pressure, decision-making, responsibility, teamwork

work_and_career.counseling: Free counseling and guidance through the Department and Fund (youth centers)

budget_tips: Work out a daily budget in advance
Separate pre-trip expenses from daily expenses
Travel insurance is a must (including extreme sports and rescue)
Check visas and vaccinations in advance
travel.funding: The discharge grant can be used for a trip. The deposit is usually not meant for travel in the first years.
travel.safety: It is recommended to register with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and stay in touch.

housing.lone_soldiers_extra: Enhanced housing rights + the option to stay in soldiers' homes for up to 3 months after discharge
housing.deposit_use: The deposit can be used to buy an apartment or land

emotional_support.normalization: Most discharged soldiers go through a period of confusion or emptiness. It is normal and does not mean something is wrong.
normalization_sentences: It is normal to feel empty or directionless after discharge.
Most discharged soldiers change direction at least once.
Most people feel more stable after 3–6 months.
You do not have to decide your whole life in the first month.

extra: Longer validity for some benefits (up to 10 years)
Rent assistance: up to 1,200 ₪ a month in the first year
Full funding of the psychometric exam registration

reservists.notes: Some rights are extended. There are dedicated benefits after long periods of reserve duty.

national_service.notes: Entitled to most benefits, sometimes in slightly different amounts.

olim.notes: Entitled to Mimadim LeLimudim and sometimes to additional benefits.

first_30_days: Check that the grant reached your account
Log in to the personal area on the Department's website
Go to a youth center for counseling if needed
Open or update your National Insurance file
Ask your employer for tax credit points (Form 101)
first_6_months: Decide on a main direction (work / studies / travel)
Complete matriculation or a mechina if missing
Check eligibility for Mimadim LeLimudim or periphery scholarships
Check eligibility for the preferred work grant
Plan how to use the deposit

decision_tree.not_sure: Start with counseling at a youth center + a talk with the companion
decision_tree.want_studies: Check Mimadim LeLimudim + the deposit + a mechina
decision_tree.want_work: Prepare a CV + check preferred work + career counseling
decision_tree.want_travel: Plan a budget from the grant + insurance + a basic route
decision_tree.feel_stuck: Emotional support + one small step for today

first_year: Check what is still valid — free public transport lasts 12 months
Apply for the preferred work grant within 42 months of discharge
Plan using the deposit within 5 years
Check that the tax credit points appear on your payslip

faq.question: When does the discharge grant arrive?
faq.answer: Usually within 60 days. Lone soldiers get an advance sooner.

faq.question: What can the deposit be used for?
faq.answer: In the first 5 years: studies, training, driving lessons, a business, an apartment, marriage. After 5 years – free.

faq.question: Who is eligible for Mimadim LeLimudim?
faq.answer: Mainly combat soldiers with a 'gold' discharge, and also lone soldiers, new immigrants and members of minority communities.

faq.question: Can the deposit be used for a trip?
faq.answer: Usually not in the first years. The grant can.

faq.question: How do I get the tax credit points?
faq.answer: Through your employer (Form 101) or tax coordination with the Tax Authority.

faq.question: What is the difference between the grant and the deposit?
faq.answer: The discharge grant is free money transferred to your bank account and can be used for anything (including travel). The personal deposit is savings meant for approved purposes (studies, driving, business, apartment, marriage) in the first 5 years, and then becomes free.

faq.question: Are tax credit points automatic?
faq.answer: No. You must request them on Form 101 with your employer. If you missed them – you can ask for a tax refund later.

faq.question: Someone offers to release my deposit early for a fee – is that okay?
faq.answer: No. It is illegal. The deposit is used only through the personal area on the Department's website, free of charge.

important_warnings: Do not pay any company that offers to "release your deposit early" — it is illegal.
Amounts change — always check the official site.
Tax credit points are not automatic — you must ask your employer for them.
grant_vs_deposit: The discharge grant is free money transferred to your bank account and can be used for any purpose (including a trip). The personal deposit is savings meant for approved purposes (studies, driving, business, apartment, marriage) in the first 5 years, and then becomes free to use.
